summary.name: Quail
summary.one_liner: Quail is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that runs local GGUF and MLX models on Apple silicon and exposes OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints for tools like Claude Code, Codex and editors.
use_cases: Serving local models to Claude Code or Codex on a Mac
Pointing editors like Zed or Continue at a local model
Running private offline chat with downloaded models
Benchmarking which models run well on your Mac
Checking whether a model fits your Mac's memory before downloading
summary.what_it_does: Quail runs a local model server from a macOS menu bar app, serving both GGUF models (via llama.cpp) and MLX models (via Apple's MLX) from one model folder. Before download, each model gets a fit verdict (Comfortable, Tight or Won't fit) and an estimated speed, and context sizes adjust to available memory. It provides copy-ready setup snippets for many tools, with a Test button, and a quail command-line interface for pulling models, chatting, benchmarking and launching tools. The server speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, Responses and Embeddings, and Anthropic Messages APIs; it keeps prompts on the Mac, defaults to answering only this machine, and enables an API key by default.
notable: Single server runs both GGUF (llama.cpp) and MLX models with fit verdicts before download
OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints so Claude Code and Codex can use local models
Homebrew cask install and self-updating, signed and notarized app
Deliberately no built-in chat window, agents, or image/audio generation
caveats: Requires macOS 14 Sonoma or later on Apple silicon
No built-in chat window; uses browser-based server chat page or quail chat
Does not do agents or image and audio generation
